subject: Private deployment: confirmation of tenant data ownership & sunset process
messages:
From: Sara Green <sara.green@fintec-example.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@fintec-example.com
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: tenancy ownership + secure deletion evidence

Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of items our compliance team asked me to confirm before we sign the Dedicated/Private order:

- For private (VPC) deployments, can you confirm that the customer retains exclusive control of persistent storage (S3 buckets, EBS, etc.) and that Redwood only writes to customer-managed volumes?
- When a tenant is decommissioned, what concrete artifacts do you provide as proof of data deletion (logs, runbook steps, checksums, timestamps)? We need to attach something to our audit.
- Do you offer a signed attestation or certificate that describes the deletion process and timelines?

If you can respond with a short list and any sample artifacts, that would speed our legal review. We may loop in our legal team (cc'd).

Appreciate it,

Sara Green
Head of Cloud Ops | FinTec Systems
Sara.Green@fintec-example.com
+1 415-555-0124

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: tenancy ownership + secure deletion evidence

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I attached a short runbook and architecture diagram for reference. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through.

- Customer-controlled storage: For Redwood Private (VPC), all persistent model and application data is written only to customer-owned volumes or object stores that you provision and manage. We support: customer-managed S3 buckets (with explicit bucket ARNs in configuration), customer EBS volumes in the VPC, or on-prem NFS mounts. By default we do not copy tenant data to Redwood-managed buckets.

- Deletion artifacts: When a tenant deletion is executed we produce:
  * Deletion runbook entry (runbook step with operator id and timestamp)
  * Orchestration job logs (task ids, exit codes)
  * Cloud provider object deletion records (S3 DeleteMarkers / ETag references)
  * Hash-sum verification of tombstoned manifests (where applicable)
  * Finalization ticket in the ops audit log (immutable entry)

- Attestation: We can provide a signed customer-specific deletion attestation PDF that states the execution dates and list of artifacts. For enterprise contracts we add this as an appendix to the DPA or as a one-off signed attestation.

Attachments included: redwood_private_data_sunset_runbook.pdf, residency-architecture-diagram.png

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a sample attestation text for legal to review.
2) If you want a documented timeline and S3 ARNs in the contract, we can add a small contract exhibit that binds to your bucket identifiers.
3) If you require HSM-backed key destruction proofs, we can coordinate a KMS export and key revocation timeline; that’s a separate run.

If that looks fine I’ll draft the attestation and loop in Legal.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: internal: sample attestation + DPA note

Rishi — quick internal:
- Legal prefers the attestation to reference the exact deletion artifacts we will hand over (runbook pdf, ops ticket id, S3 deletion markers). Avoid generic phrasing like "we deleted all copies".
- Can we prepare the attestation as a templated PDF that can be populated with the bucket ARNs + timestamps before signature? That speeds turnaround.
- Also confirm whether the runbook contains step-level operator IDs or only job ids; FinTec will want operator-level auditability.

I can draft the tagging language for the DPA exhibit; will need R&D to confirm whether we retain any ephemeral internal cache beyond the customer-managed storage (we should call it out explicitly).

Thanks — L

Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: tenancy ownership + secure deletion evidence

Sara — following up with a concise, customer-ready summary and the promised artifacts. See inline and attachments.

SUMMARY (customer-facing)
- Storage ownership: Redwood Private writes to customer-provisioned volumes only. We can confirm ARNs/volume IDs in the contract exhibit.
- Deletion run: When you request tenant decommissioning our orchestration executes the documented runbook; outputs include orchestration job logs, S3 deletion markers, and an immutable ops audit entry. If you request a full forensic pack we include job logs, deletion timestamps, and checksums where available.
- Attestation: Attached is a draft attestation template we sign after execution. We can attach final ARNs and timestamps and deliver the signed PDF.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- redwood_private_data_sunset_runbook.pdf (operator steps + artifacts produced)
- residency-architecture-diagram.png (deployment sketch showing customer-owned buckets/volumes)
- dpa-amendment-docusign.url (link stub to the DPA amendment prepared for FinTec)

Notes on ephemeral caches: We maintain an in-memory KV cache for latency-sensitive workloads inside the deployment; the cache is non-persistent and flushed on service restart. We do not persist KV cache to Redwood-managed storage in Private/VPC mode. If you require an explicit cache-clear event as part of deletion we can include that as a runbook step and log it.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the bucket ARNs or volume IDs you want us to include.
2) Legal: if the DPA exhibit language looks acceptable, we’ll populate and route via DocuSign (link attached).
3) If you want operator-level audit trail, tell us the retention window required and we’ll confirm the operator id capture in the runbook (aditya_rao and infra will validate).
